newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark says good progress in Monday talks.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark says good progress in Monday talks.

text.p: Labour leader Helen Clark said the party made "very fast progress" in its latest coalition talks with New Zealand First on Monday but confirmed it did not yet have an outline deal to show to Tuesday's party caucus.
She told reporters it remained to be seen whether Labour may hold a special caucus later in the week to discuss a coalition deal.
"We were able to make very fast progress today because everybody had the time to read the papers that had been drafted," Clark said after the three-hour meeting.

A New Zealand First spokesman said the party was still hopeful of reaching a coalition agreement with either Labour or the caretaker National Party government in time for the resumption of parliament.
Parliament must meet by December 13 for the first time since the inconclusive October 12 general election.
